reviewed_finding: The source declarations are l1_residual_sector_weights_minimizer_nonuniqueness_and_dihedral_selector (fixed rA=(1,1,0,0), rB=(0,0,1,1), plus a conjunct that is true for any w0,w1 and uses neither), even_cycle_sector_weights_require_selector (two fixed C4 vectors by decide), l1_even_cycle_symmetry_orbit_canonical_sector_weights (fixed vectors by decide; the orbit SUM has twice Phi1) and sector_weights_sum_to_phi1 (additivity of a list sum on append). None of them defines the minimum over a class, so "Phi1" there is the L1 of a given residual. The general claim is therefore proved afresh: on the n-cycle the class is the holonomy, Phi1 = |S|, the minimizers are a signed simplex, two minimizers with equal (Phi1, Gamma2) differ in sector weights, and the symmetric average is an extra declared selector (integral only when n divides S). Weighted L1 forms are not treated.

claim_boundary.supports: On the n-cycle with the unweighted (equal edge mass) L1 form (kernel-checked for every n, every cochain c, over every commutative linearly ordered ring incl. Int and Rat): the class of c in C^1/im d0 is determined by the holonomy S = sum c; Phi1(c) = min_h L1(c - d0 h) = |S| and is attained; the minimizers are exactly the cochains with sum S all of whose entries have the sign of S (a scaled simplex); for n >= 2 and S != 0 two minimizers share Phi1 and the holonomy S but differ as residuals and in the weights of any bipartition into two nonempty sectors, so the sector weights are NOT a function of (Phi1, Gamma2), where Gamma2 is MODELLED as the holonomy (class invariant) as in the TFQ-0354 M1 syndrome; the repo PUB-009 witness uses Gamma_2 = sum w_i^2, and under that reading the minimizers do not even share Gamma2 (native: sum of squares ranges from sumsq_min to sumsq_max, e.g. 2 to 4 for the class (1,0,1,0)), but that reading is not a Lean anchor; the weights of the two sectors always add up to Phi1; S = 0 forces the zero residual (total mass 0, refused by the node) and n = 1 has a unique minimizer; the cyclically invariant minimizer exists and is unique over a field (constant S/n) and is integral iff n divides S, so it is a separate declared selector. Native (exact enumeration, not kernel theorems): 16 unweighted cases incl. S = 0, S < 0, n = 1 and a single sector; 6 WEIGHTED cases with declared integer masses showing that the minimizer lives on the minimal-mass edges (unique when the minimum is attained once, so the sector weights can then be determined by the declared masses, and determined-but-not-unique when all minimal edges share a sector); and 4 two-disjoint-cycle cases (cycle rank 2) where one total holonomy does not determine Phi1.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Any derivation of declared sector weights from Phi1 and Gamma2 in the setting of the node source: the result is specific to EQUAL edge masses; for a weighted L1 form with a unique minimal-mass edge the minimizer, hence the sector weights, are unique (native weighted rows), so non-derivability can fail in the weighted setting that the node source declares (the masses are then the declared input); a Lean proof of the weighted statement or of the sum-of-squares reading of Gamma2; connected graphs of cycle rank > 1 (only two DISJOINT cycles are tabulated natively); the Hilbert lift, density matrices or any physical reading of the weights; that the dihedral or cyclic symmetry is itself available (it is an extra declared input).
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For the n-cycle with the unweighted L1 form, the set of minimizing residuals is the scaled simplex of sign-definite cochains with sum S (minimizer_iff); the sector weights are its block sums, which are not a function of (Phi1, Gamma2 = holonomy) for n >= 2, S != 0 and at least two sectors (sector_weights_not_determined), because (Phi1, Gamma2) determine only the signed holonomy S (hence Phi1 = |S| and the sign pattern); any single choice, including the cyclically symmetric average S/n, is an extra declaration, and with unequal declared masses the minimizer concentrates on the minimal-mass edges (native rows) so the masses themselves are the declared input.
claim_boundary.next_test: Prove in the kernel that for the weighted form sum_i m_i |r_i| with declared positive edge masses the minimizers on the n-cycle are exactly the sign-definite cochains of holonomy S supported on the edges of minimal mass, so that the weights are unique iff the minimal mass is attained once.

second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T132245Z_staged. I recompiled lean4/ResidualSectorWeights.lean (Lean 4.35.0, all 14 anchors on propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only); production and p1 construction copies of Lean/Python/Rust are byte-identical; checker sha equals the p2 pin. Anchor fidelity: the module is over CommRing+LinearOrder+IsStrictOrderedRing (covers Int, Rat). class_iff (class = holonomy), phi1_attained_and_lower_bound (|hol| lower bound, attained), minimizer_iff (exactly the sign-definite cochains of the right holonomy), minimizers_not_unique and sector_weights_not_determined (for ANY subset A with i in A, j not in A, hol c != 0: two minimizers with equal l1 and equal hol but different A-weight; more general than the checker's contiguous blocks), sector_weights_sum_to_phi1 (any A), minimizer_unique_of_hol_zero, minimizer_unique_of_one_edge, symmetric_integral_iff and symmetric_selector (unique rotation-invariant minimizer hol/n over a field) all say what supports says. The C4 theorems are labelled instances. Earlier-pass amendments: all applied in the final text. Gamma2 is now stated as MODELLED as the holonomy, with the PUB-009 sum-of-squares reading declared not a Lean anchor (does_not_support also lists a Lean proof of the sum-of-squares reading); narrowest_claim now says 'minimizing residuals ... scaled simplex (minimizer_iff); sector weights are its block sums' and 'determine only the signed holonomy S'; does_not_support now says the result is specific to EQUAL edge masses and may fail in the weighted setting; semantic mutants weighted_l1_treated_as_unweighted, gamma2_as_sum_of_squares_constant_on_minimizers, cycle_rank_two_single_holonomy and determined_but_not_unique_read_as_free are present and rejected; 6 weighted and 4 two-cycle native rows exist. 1349 coordinate + 14 semantic mutants rejected. New observations. (1) Modelling identification not named: the module DEFINES the weight of a sector A as sum_{e in A} |r_e| for a residual r in the class c - d0 h on an n-cycle, and Phi1 as the minimum of the L1 form over that class. The source (declared residual sector masses mu(s), Phi1 and Gamma2 of the Phi1/Gamma2 residual) is not reproduced in Lean; this identification does not appear in does_not_support. (2) In the weighted rows the recorded sector_vectors are UNWEIGHTED block sums of |r| (masses (5,2,2), class (2,-3,0): weighted_phi1 = 2 but sector vector (0,1) sums to 1), so for weighted rows the 'sector weights add up to Phi1' sentence does not hold in the recorded coordinates. Because every weighted minimizer lives on minimal-mass edges (the checker asserts this), mass-weighted block sums are m_min times the recorded ones and the determined/unique flags are unaffected; the convention should be stated, as should the restriction to positive masses. (3) The 'symmetric' field is the per-edge WEIGHT |S|/n, while the Lean selector is the signed cochain hol c / n (for S = -3, n = 4 the record says 3/4, the Lean constant is -3/4). (4) Gamma2 sentence: 'under that reading the minimizers do not even share Gamma2' is true of the whole minimizer set, but the single-edge pair S e_i, S e_j DOES share sum |r|^2 = S^2, and with exactly two sectors (Phi1, sum w^2) fixes the weight pair up to order (w0 w1 = (P^2-Q)/2), so under that reading non-determination of the ordered vector is a swap artifact for two sectors and only a real statement for >= 3 sectors. The reading is correctly left unpaid, but the sentence could suggest 'worse' rather than 'different'. (5) Checker leniency: type equality is checked only at the top level (type(r[k]) is type(want[k])), so True is accepted for 1 inside nested lists. I confirmed this by running the checker on a temporary copy of the candidate with true in lex_max, symmetric and sector_vectors: it printed records_checked 26. The sealed certificate itself is correct and passes exact Python/Rust wire equality, so this is not a defect of the sealed bytes, but the element-wise type checks present in L1-QM122 (is_int) and L1-U1-SELECTOR (one-level element check) are missing here. (6) The checker line 'n*sym == best' is tautological (sym is defined as best/n). Checker independence: strong. It enumerates c - d0 h over a gauge-fixed box with a justified bound (unweighted |h_i| <= 2 sum|c|; weighted |h_i| <= sum|c| + floor(sum m|c| / m_min)), reads off minimum, full minimizer set, lex extremes, block-sum tuples and sum-of-squares extremes, and only then asserts holonomy invariance, sign, minimal-mass support and weighted minimum = |S| m_min as theorem-level cross-checks; the producer uses closed forms. No hard-coded certificate values. next_test (kernel proof for the weighted form: minimizers supported on minimal-mass edges, weights unique iff the minimal mass is attained once) is the node's own unpaid obligation and acceptable. DAG: the node statement is an absence/declaration claim ('no derivation of w from Phi1/Gamma2 is given in the sources read'), PROVED_LEAN rested on fixed C4 instances; the new theorem narrows to the unweighted n-cycle model, which is not the weighted-mass setting the source declares, so I support lowering the status.

earlier_pass.notes: I recompiled lean4/ResidualSectorWeights.lean (Lean 4.35.0, exit 0, all 14 anchors on propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only) and the p1 construction copies are byte-identical to production. The anchors state what they are said to state: class_iff (class = holonomy), phi1_attained_and_lower_bound (|hol| lower bound, attained), minimizer_iff (sign-definite cochains of the right holonomy), minimizers_not_unique / sector_weights_not_determined (for ARBITRARY subset A with i in A, j not in A and hol c != 0, two minimizers with equal l1 and hol and different sector weight on A, which is more general than the checker's contiguous blocks), minimizer_unique_of_hol_zero, minimizer_unique_of_one_edge (Fin 1), symmetric_integral_iff, symmetric_selector (unique rotation-invariant minimizer hol/n over a field). All are over CommRing+LinearOrder+IsStrictOrderedRing, so Int and Rat are covered. The two C4 instances are genuinely labelled as instances. WEAKNESSES. (1) Gamma2. The claim says minimizers 'share Phi1 and Gamma2 (= S)'. In the repo's own PUB-009 witness (derivation_dag_witnesses.rs line ~274-280) Gamma_2 = sum of w_i^2 (second moment of the weight vector, Xi = Phi1^2/Gamma2), whereas TFQ-0354's M1 receipt uses 'holonomy_gamma2'. The Lean module never defines Gamma2; it identifies it with hol silently. Under the sum-of-squares reading the same witnesses (S e_i vs S e_j) also have equal sum |r|^2 = S^2, so the conclusion survives, but that equality is not stated in any anchor nor checked. The profile must say that Gamma2 is MODELLED as the holonomy and that the sum-of-squares reading is unchecked. (2) The narrowest_claim says 'the set of minimizing sector-weight vectors is the scaled simplex'. The kernel proves the minimizers are the scaled simplex of cochains (minimizer_iff) and that sector weights are not a function of (Phi1, hol); it does not state that the set of sector-weight vectors is the full simplex over the sectors (block-sum image), nor that over Int it is the lattice points. The checker confirms it only on 16 cases by enumeration. Soften to 'the minimizers form the scaled simplex of cochains; sector weights are the block sums of that simplex'. 'Determine only the total |S|' is also loose: they determine the signed S and the sign pattern of every minimizer. (3) The decisive unpaid bridge is understated. The source is about a WEIGHTED window norm with declared masses mu(s). With unequal positive edge masses the minimizer of sum m_i |r_i| on a class with holonomy S is concentrated on the minimal-mass edge(s): UNIQUE whenever the minimum mass is attained once. So the equal-mass (unweighted) non-uniqueness is a special case and does not carry over: for a weighted form the sector weights can in fact be determined by the masses (themselves a declaration). does_not_support mentions the weighted form but says only that the minimizer set 'changes and may be a face or a point'; it should say plainly that the non-derivability result is specific to equal edge masses and may fail (be unique) in the weighted setting that the node's source actually uses. This is why I recommend lowering the DAG status. CHECKER. Independent and strong: it enumerates c - d0 h over a gauge-fixed box with a justified bound (|h_i| <= 2 sum|c|, valid), reads min, full minimizer set, lex extremes and sector-weight tuples from the enumeration, checks holonomy invariance and sign of every enumerated minimizer, recomputes the symmetric point in exact rationals; the producer uses closed forms. All leaves are compared with exact types; no tolerance. It tests only contiguous-block sectors (Lean is more general). MUTANTS. Mostly genuine and well targeted: unique_minimizer_from_one_witness (instance read as general), orbit_sum_as_symmetric_point (the source's own error), rounded_symmetric_point, raw_l1_read_as_phi1, sign swap, minimizers counted by sector vectors (3 vs 10) are real near misses. zero_mass_accepted, holonomy_as_absolute_value are flag edits. Missing near misses: (a) weighted L1 treated as unweighted (unequal masses, unique minimizer at the min-mass edge); (b) Gamma2 read as sum of squares with a pair of minimizers of different sum of squares (e.g. (2,0) vs (1,1) on sizes 2,2: Gamma2 4 vs 2) to show the two readings of Gamma2 give different 'fibers'; (c) a graph with cycle rank > 1 (class not determined by one holonomy). next_test (weighted L1 with declared masses, decide whether the masses select a face) is this node's own obligation and is distinct from does_not_support only in being a computation rather than an exclusion; acceptable. DAG: the DAG statement is an absence claim ('no derivation is given in the sources read'), which no theorem can discharge; the label PROVED_LEAN rested on fixed C4 instances. The new theorem narrows it to the unweighted n-cycle model, which is not the model the node's source uses, so I would lower the status.
